obligations.summary: Each Member State shall establish or designate at least one notifying authority and at least one market surveillance authority as national competent authorities, ensuring they exercise their powers independently, impartially and without bias.
exceptions: Activities and tasks may be performed by one or more designated authorities in accordance with the organisational needs of the Member State, provided principles of independence and impartiality are observed.

obligations.summary: Member States shall communicate to the Commission the identity and tasks of their notifying and market surveillance authorities, make contact information publicly available by 2 August 2025, designate a single point of contact, and notify the Commission of its identity.

Member States shall ensure their national competent authorities are provided with adequate technical, financial, human resources and infrastructure, including personnel with expertise in AI, data, cybersecurity, fundamental rights, health and safety, and shall assess and update these requirements annually.
National competent authorities shall take appropriate measures to ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity.
National competent authorities shall act in accordance with the confidentiality obligations set out in Article 78 when performing their tasks.
Member States shall report to the Commission by 2 August 2025, and every two years thereafter, on the status and adequacy of the financial and human resources of their national competent authorities.
The Commission shall facilitate the exchange of experience between national competent authorities.

National competent authorities may provide guidance and advice on the implementation of this Regulation, particularly to SMEs and start-ups, and shall consult competent authorities under other Union law when guidance concerns AI systems in areas covered by that other Union law.
exceptions: Consultation with other Union law competent authorities is required only where guidance relates to AI systems in areas covered by that other Union law.

obligations.summary: Where Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies fall within the scope of this Regulation, the European Data Protection Supervisor shall act as the competent authority for their supervision.
